name: Medusa
title: Medusa SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Medusa’s Store API: setup, environment and settings. 31 of 43 services wired, but cart and sign-in are not, so it cannot sell yet.
lede: The Medusa connector reaches Medusa’s Store API with a publishable key and a region. Its guide describes cart, checkout and sign-in as Medusa-native, but the coverage script does not count cart or sign-in as wired — and until that is settled, it cannot sell.
verdict: Cannot sell yet. The coverage script counts cart and sign-in — and products, categories and search — as not wired, and CONNECTORS.md says this connector predates the current wiring pass and has not had the source-verification sweep the others have. Even by its own guide, only cash on delivery completes: the card gateways still post to Litekart endpoints.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Medusa server

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_MEDUSA_API_URL
env.note: Base URL of the Medusa server’s Store API.

env.name: PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_API_KEY
env.note: A publishable API key created in the Medusa admin. Publishable keys are meant to be used from a browser.

env.name: PUBLIC_MEDUSA_REGION_ID
env.note: The region ID (`reg_…`) used for pricing, currency and availability.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/medusa-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: Boot checks only `PUBLIC_MEDUSA_API_URL`, but the guide marks all three as required. The Litekart trio is not used in Medusa mode.
backendSettings: Create a publishable API key in the Medusa admin and set it as `PUBLIC_MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_API_KEY`.
Add the storefront’s origin to Medusa’s Store CORS configuration.
howItWorks: At boot, `init` in both hooks (through `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts`) writes the three `PUBLIC_MEDUSA_*` values onto the connector’s `BaseService` — `BASE_URL`, `PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `REGION_ID`. The server hook covers server rendering; the client hook covers the browser, which must reach the public Medusa URL in production.

By the guide’s account, cart, shipping rates and payment-method listing are Medusa-native; sign-in, sign-up, sign-out and password reset go through the Medusa SDK; categories map to Medusa product categories; and the profile page delegates to Medusa’s `getMe` and `updateProfile`. Medusa needs an email on the cart to complete an order, so the static store config defaults `isEmailMandatory` to `true`.

Store identity, menus and plugin toggles are static — `default-store.json` under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts` — and CMS pages and the blog resolve empty. From connector 2.1.6 the REST paths it once inherited from Litekart are answered by the connector itself.

The coverage script and the guide disagree. The script counts a service as wired only if it reaches the connector’s own HTTP layer, and it does not count cart, auth, product, category, search, address, user or payment-method. CONNECTORS.md names Medusa and Saleor as the next candidates for the source-verification sweep.
limitations: Sign-in (auth): not wired — the coverage script does not count it, though the guide describes email sign-in as native.
Cart: not wired — the coverage script does not count it, though the guide describes the cart as Medusa-native.

The card gateways in this connector — Razorpay, Stripe, PhonePe, PayPal, Cashfree, Affirm — still post to Litekart `/api/checkout/*` endpoints and will not work without a Litekart API. Only cash on delivery completes through Medusa.
OTP sign-in is a mock: `getOtp` reports success without sending anything.
Legal and CMS pages render their layout with empty content; the wishlist and the cart’s coupon drawer show empty states.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden in Medusa mode without firing requests.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_MEDUSA_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: The variable is set while a different connector is installed. Install `@misiki/medusa-connector`, or remove the variable if you meant to run another backend. With more than one connector installed, set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/medusa-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/medusa-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: `[medusa] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Medusa has no such feature; if it has one, implement it in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so neither its guard nor `blockRestFallbacks` saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong branding
troubleshooting.fix: Set identity overrides — `name`, `logo`, `favicon`, `currencyCode` and the rest — in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in or cart works in dev but not when deployed
troubleshooting.fix: Check the publishable API key, and that the deployed storefront’s origin is in Medusa’s Store CORS configuration.

faq.q: Can I sell on Medusa with Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Not yet. The coverage script counts the cart and sign-in as not wired, and CONNECTORS.md says the Medusa connector predates the current wiring pass. By its own guide, only cash on delivery completes; the card gateways still post to Litekart endpoints.

faq.q: Why does the guide say the cart works when the coverage table says it does not?
faq.a: They measure different things. The guide describes what the connector calls; the coverage script counts a service only when it reaches the connector’s own HTTP layer, and does not count cart, auth, products, categories or search. CONNECTORS.md lists Medusa as a next candidate for the source-verification sweep that would settle it.

faq.q: What does Medusa need configured for Svelte Commerce?
faq.a: A publishable API key created in the Medusa admin, a region ID for pricing and currency, and the storefront’s origin in Medusa’s Store CORS configuration.

faq.q: Which payment methods work with Medusa?
faq.a: Cash on delivery completes through the Medusa SDK. The card gateways in this connector — Razorpay, Stripe, PhonePe, PayPal, Cashfree, Affirm — still post to Litekart endpoints and do not work without a Litekart API.
